consequence: PASS:C2 under the registered bootstrap/Holm rule: RELAY_START_POLICY=edges and RELAY_READAHEAD_POLICY=upstream become the defaults in a separate commit; the legacy values stay selectable for rollback.
analysis: C2 improves time-to-start in 5 of 6 key cells after Holm (fast/1MiB not significant): fast/16MiB 12.6 -> 9.0 s, fast/4MiB 6.4 -> 4.5 s, thin/16MiB 14.1 -> 11.5 s, thin/4MiB 9.8 -> 6.7 s, thin/1MiB 6.3 -> 5.5 s (means, n=10); also at 8 and 60 Mbit/s on fast (-1.7 to -3.3 s). No regression after Holm over 48 guard tests; 0 failed runs, 0 application-frame tracebacks.

Residual uncertainty, reported openly: post-seek resume with 16 MiB pieces is +0.2 to +0.7 s on the fast profile (raw one-sided p 0.0015-0.0035 at 8/60 Mbit/s, above the Holm threshold of ~0.001 for 48 tests) and mixed/4MiB +0.57 s (p 0.0035). Upstream (pb1-v1, pb0-v2) shows the same small seek cost with 16 MiB pieces, so this is the known price of the upstream start order, not a new defect.
C4 (edges alone) improved all 6 key cells but failed on one significant seek regression (fast/16MiB/8Mbit +1.22 s, p 0.0005); C2's upstream deadline formula keeps the seek cost lower.
